title: Health providers under one owner, billing under several names
question: Which Medicare-enrolled providers with a San Francisco address share an owner with a differently named provider in the Bay Area?
finding: 6 groups of two or more differently named Bay Area providers, each with at least one San Francisco address, are joined by owner numbers in the federal enrolment file; 4 have two or more names in San Francisco itself and 1 have two names at one street address. The largest holds 32 provider names and 96 billing numbers (Bay Area Master Tenant Llc; Bay Bridge Capital Partners, Llc; Hudson River Opco Llc; Pacs Group, Inc. and 4 more organizations). 3 of the groups include an owner already on the list in the “health” results; what this screen adds is the restriction to ownership interests and the count of names and billing numbers per group.
how: From the federal enrolment owners extract already used by the “health” results, only rows where the owner holds an ownership interest or is a partner are kept (officers, directors and managing employees are dropped). Owners are identified by the federal owner number, not by name. Providers are gathered into one group wherever an owner number appears on two of them, so a chain held through layers of holding companies is one row; a group is listed if it has two or more differently named enrolments in the Bay Area counties and at least one in San Francisco. Billing numbers are the distinct provider, certification and enrolment numbers in the set.
limits: Chains are disclosed to Medicare in exactly this file, so nothing here is hidden from the payer; the screen shows where separate provider names and numbers are one business, which matters when reading the address clusters in the “health” results and the site’s “Hospices, nursing homes and prescribers” page. Only provider types with an ownership file on disk are covered (nursing homes, home health agencies, hospices, hospitals, and federally qualified and rural health clinics); physician groups, pharmacies, laboratories and equipment suppliers have none. Individuals are shown as codes. Some provider names in the federal extract are garbled (for example names ending "idence Opco") and are printed as the file gives them; the source looks wrong there, not the provider.
